summary.text: Laurel Lee is the Republican incumbent in Florida's 15th Congressional District, first elected in 2022. An attorney, she worked as a federal public defender and federal prosecutor, served as a Hillsborough County circuit judge, and was Florida's Secretary of State from 2019 to 2022. Her Republican primary in 2026 was canceled.

paragraphs.text: Born at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio and raised in a military family; her office says she is the daughter of a two-star U.S. Air Force general.
Earned a bachelor's degree in political science from the University of Florida in 1996 and a law degree from the University of Florida in 1999.
Worked as a law clerk to Judge James S. Moody of the U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Florida and as an attorney with Carlton Fields, P.A.

Served as an assistant federal public defender and then as an assistant U.S. attorney in the Middle District of Florida, where her office says she handled False Claims Act cases and criminal prosecutions.
Served as a judge of Florida's Thirteenth Judicial Circuit Court in Hillsborough County from 2013 to 2019, appointed by Gov. Rick Scott.
Served as Florida's 36th Secretary of State under Gov. Ron DeSantis from January 2019 to May 2022.
Won the 2022 general election for Florida's 15th District, defeating Alan Cohn, and was sworn in on January 3, 2023; she was re-elected in 2024, defeating Pat Kemp.
Serves on the House Energy and Commerce, Judiciary, and Administration Committees; her office says she introduced the REINS Act in her first week in office.
Her office says she lives in eastern Hillsborough County with her husband, Tom, and their three children.
